- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in downward trends.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct quickly — overcorrects downward in subsequent periods.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reversion suggests.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, especially when history includes recent highs.
- Model underreacts to sharp downward corrections in the middle of the forecast horizon — fails to anticipate sudden drops.
- When true price drops below 70, model often fails to adjust downward sufficiently, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecast exhibits “sticky” behavior — resistant to change when true price moves sharply, especially after a spike.
